lessons.title: Basic Greetings
lessons.description: Learn standard English greetings like Hello, Good Morning, and how to respond politely.

learn.meaning: A common greeting used to start a conversation.
learn.example: Hello! How are you today?

learn.meaning: A polite greeting used from sunrise until noon.
learn.example: Good morning, team! Let's start the meeting.

learn.meaning: A polite greeting used from noon until early evening.
learn.example: Good afternoon, sir. How can I help you?

learn.meaning: A polite greeting used in the evening hours.
learn.example: Good evening, everyone. Welcome to the event.

learn.meaning: A phrase used when leaving or saying farewell.
learn.example: Goodbye! Have a wonderful weekend.

learn.meaning: A polite word used to ask for something nicely.
learn.example: Could you pass the salt, please?

practice.title: Listen & Repeat
practice.subtitle: Listen to the audio and repeat to improve your pronunciation.

practice.title: Fill in the Blanks
practice.subtitle: Complete the sentences with the correct words.
practice.sentence: Good _______, everyone! Have a great morning.

practice.title: Speak Yourself
practice.subtitle: Practice speaking and record your voice.
practice.aiPrompt: You are a friendly AI English tutor. The student is practicing basic greetings. Respond to their greeting (e.g. 'Hello', 'Good morning') with a warm, encouraging greeting of your own and ask a simple follow-up question.

quiz.question: Which greeting is used in the morning?
What is a polite way to say goodbye?
Which word is used to show politeness when requesting something?
What is the correct response to 'How are you?'
When do we say 'Good Evening'?

review.summary: You have completed Lesson 1! You can now confidently greet others, use polite expressions, and respond to basic everyday greetings.

lessons.title: Introducing Yourself
lessons.description: Learn how to state your name, ask for someone else's name, and say 'Nice to meet you'.

learn.meaning: To present someone or yourself by name to others.
learn.example: Let me introduce myself: my name is Sarah.

learn.meaning: A word by which a person, place, or thing is known.
learn.example: What is your name?

learn.meaning: To come into the presence or company of someone.
learn.example: It is nice to meet you.

learn.meaning: A warm greeting given to a newcomer.
learn.example: Welcome to our English class!

learn.meaning: A person whom one knows and has a bond of mutual affection with.
learn.example: This is my friend, John.

learn.meaning: The nation where a person lives or was born.
learn.example: Which country are you from?

practice.title: Listen & Repeat
practice.subtitle: Listen to the audio and repeat to improve your pronunciation.
practice.phrase: My name is John. Nice to meet you.

practice.title: Fill in the Blanks
practice.subtitle: Complete the sentences with the correct words.

practice.title: Speak Yourself
practice.subtitle: Practice speaking and record your voice.
practice.aiPrompt: You are a friendly AI English tutor. Ask the student for their name and country. When they introduce themselves, respond warmly, tell them your name (WeBot), and say 'Nice to meet you!'

quiz.question: What is the standard response after someone introduces themselves?
How do you ask for someone's name?
What is a 'friend'?
options: A person you know and like

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: '_______ to our class!'
What does 'introduce' mean?

review.summary: You have completed Lesson 2! You now know how to introduce yourself, state your name, share where you are from, and greet new people politely.

lessons.title: Talking About Family
lessons.description: Learn the words for common family members like father, mother, brother, and sister.

learn.meaning: A group of parents and children living together.
learn.example: I love spending time with my family.

learn.meaning: A male parent.
learn.example: My father is a teacher.

learn.meaning: A female parent.
learn.example: My mother cooked a delicious dinner.

learn.meaning: A male sibling.
learn.example: I have one older brother.

learn.meaning: A female sibling.
learn.example: My sister is studying at university.

learn.meaning: A person's father and mother.
learn.example: My parents live in London.

practice.title: Listen & Repeat
practice.subtitle: Listen to the audio and repeat to improve your pronunciation.
practice.phrase: I have a brother and a sister.

practice.title: Fill in the Blanks
practice.subtitle: Complete the sentences with the correct words.
practice.sentence: My father and mother are my _______.

practice.title: Speak Yourself
practice.subtitle: Practice speaking and record your voice.
practice.aiPrompt: You are a friendly AI English tutor. Ask the student to tell you about their family members. Ask questions like 'How many brothers or sisters do you have?' and encourage them to use vocabulary like father, mother, sister, or brother.

quiz.question: What do we call our mother and father together?
What is a female sibling called?
What is a male sibling called?
Which word represents a male parent?
Which word represents a female parent?

review.summary: You have completed Lesson 3! You can now talk about your family members and describe basic familial relationships in English.

lessons.title: Asking for Directions
lessons.description: Learn essential phrases to ask for help when navigating, such as 'Where is...?' and 'Go straight'.

learn.meaning: At, in, or to which place or position.
learn.example: Where is the nearest restroom?

learn.meaning: To change direction towards the left side.
learn.example: Turn left at the next traffic light.

learn.meaning: To change direction towards the right side.
learn.example: Go straight, then turn right at the corner.

learn.meaning: To proceed ahead without turning.
learn.example: Go straight down this street for two blocks.

learn.meaning: A place where passenger trains or buses regularly stop.
learn.example: Excuse me, where is the train station?

learn.meaning: An establishment that provides lodging for travelers.
learn.example: I am staying at the Grand Hotel.

practice.title: Listen & Repeat
practice.subtitle: Listen to the audio and repeat to improve your pronunciation.
practice.phrase: Excuse me, where is the train station?

practice.title: Fill in the Blanks
practice.subtitle: Complete the sentences with the correct words.
practice.sentence: Go straight and then turn _______ to the left side.

practice.title: Speak Yourself
practice.subtitle: Practice speaking and record your voice.
practice.aiPrompt: You are a helpful pedestrian in New York. The student will ask you for directions to the station or hotel. Give them a simple, clear set of instructions like 'Go straight for two blocks, then turn right. The station is on your left.'

quiz.question: What is the opposite of 'Turn Left'?
What question word is used to ask about a location?
What does 'Go straight' mean?
Where do passenger trains stop?
What is a polite way to get someone's attention before asking directions?

review.summary: You have completed Lesson 4! You can now ask for directions to local landmarks and understand basic directions like turning left, right, and going straight.

lessons.title: Numbers & Telling Time
lessons.description: Learn numbers 1-20, telling time, and asking 'What time is it?'.

learn.meaning: The progress of existence as measured in hours, minutes, and seconds.
learn.example: What time is it?

learn.meaning: A period of time equal to 60 minutes.
learn.example: The meeting will start in one hour.

learn.meaning: A period of time equal to 60 seconds.
learn.example: Wait a minute, please.

learn.meaning: Used to specify the hour of the day.
learn.example: It is exactly three o'clock.

learn.meaning: 30 minutes past the designated hour.
learn.example: We will meet at half past four.

learn.meaning: 15 minutes before or after the hour.
learn.example: It is a quarter to five.

practice.title: Listen & Repeat
practice.subtitle: Listen to the audio and repeat to improve your pronunciation.

practice.title: Fill in the Blanks
practice.subtitle: Complete the sentences with the correct words.
practice.sentence: What _______ is it? It is two o'clock.

practice.title: Speak Yourself
practice.subtitle: Practice speaking and record your voice.
practice.aiPrompt: You are a friendly AI English tutor. Ask the student what time they usually wake up or eat dinner. Validate their answer and practice time vocabulary like 'o'clock', 'half past', and 'minutes'.

quiz.question: What does 'half past seven' mean in numbers?
How many minutes are in an hour?
How do you ask about the current time?
What does 'quarter to six' mean?
What does 'ten o'clock' mean?

review.summary: You have completed Lesson 5! You now know how to count, tell the time, ask for the time, and use phrases like 'half past' and 'quarter to'.

lessons.title: Daily Routine
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary and verbs used to describe common actions throughout your day.

learn.meaning: To emerge or cause to emerge from sleep.
learn.example: I wake up at 6:00 AM every day.

learn.meaning: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.
learn.example: I usually eat eggs and toast for breakfast.

learn.meaning: An act of washing oneself in a shower.
learn.example: I take a quick shower before going to work.

learn.meaning: Activity involving mental or physical effort done in order to achieve a purpose.
learn.example: I walk to work every morning.

learn.meaning: Physical activity that is done in order to become stronger and healthier.
learn.example: I exercise at the gym after work.

learn.meaning: A condition of body and mind which typically recurs for several hours.
learn.example: I go to sleep at 10 PM.

practice.subtitle: Listen to the audio and repeat to improve your pronunciation.
practice.phrase: I eat breakfast and then go to work.

practice.title: Fill in the Blanks
practice.subtitle: Complete the sentences with the correct words.

practice.title: Speak Yourself
practice.subtitle: Practice speaking and record your voice.
practice.aiPrompt: You are a friendly AI English tutor. Ask the student about their typical daily routine. Ask questions like 'What do you do in the morning?' and encourage them to describe their day step by step.

quiz.question: What is the first meal of the day called?
What is the opposite of waking up?
Which verb means to wash yourself standing up under water spray?
When do people typically eat breakfast?
What do you do at a gym to stay healthy?

review.summary: You have completed Lesson 6! You are now able to describe your daily routine, morning activities, and everyday habits.

lessons.title: Ordering Food
lessons.description: Learn food vocabulary and how to interact with a waiter in a restaurant.

learn.meaning: A list of dishes available in a restaurant.
learn.example: May I please see the menu?

learn.meaning: To request food or drink in a restaurant.
learn.example: Are you ready to order?

learn.meaning: A clear liquid that is necessary for life.
learn.example: Could I get a glass of water, please?

learn.meaning: A printed list showing how much you must pay.
learn.example: Could we have the bill, please?

learn.meaning: Highly pleasant to the taste.
learn.example: This pasta is absolutely delicious!

learn.meaning: Sweet food eaten at the end of a meal.
learn.example: I would like chocolate cake for dessert.

practice.title: Listen & Repeat
practice.subtitle: Listen to the audio and repeat to improve your pronunciation.
practice.phrase: I would like to order the chicken pasta, please.

practice.title: Fill in the Blanks
practice.subtitle: Complete the sentences with the correct words.

practice.title: Speak Yourself
practice.subtitle: Practice speaking and record your voice.

quiz.question: What do you ask for when you want to choose what to eat?
What is 'dessert'?
options: Sweet food at the end of a meal

quiz.question: What do you say to the waiter when you are ready to pay?
Which word is a synonym for 'very tasty'?
How do you request water politely?
options: Could I have some water, please?

review.summary: You have completed Lesson 7! You can now order food in a restaurant, talk to waitstaff, ask for the menu and the bill, and express your preferences.

lessons.title: Shopping & Prices
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary for clothing, items, and asking 'How much does this cost?'.

learn.meaning: The amount of money needed to buy something.
learn.example: How much does this shirt cost?

learn.meaning: The amount of money expected, required, or given in payment.
learn.example: The price of this bag is fifty dollars.

learn.meaning: A deduction from the usual cost of something.
learn.example: Is there any discount on these shoes?

learn.meaning: A standard measurement of clothing.
learn.example: Do you have this dress in a medium size?

learn.meaning: To obtain in exchange for payment.
learn.example: I want to buy a new phone.

learn.meaning: Money in coins or bills, rather than cards.
learn.example: Will you pay by cash or credit card?

practice.title: Fill in the Blanks

lessons.title: Weather & Seasons

learn.meaning: Having a great deal of rainfall.

learn.meaning: Of or at a low temperature.

learn.meaning: The warmest season of the year.
learn.example: I love going to the beach in the summer.

learn.meaning: The coldest season of the year.
learn.example: It snows a lot during the winter.

lessons.title: Hobbies & Free Time
lessons.description: Learn to talk about your favorite leisure activities, sports, and what you do for fun.

learn.meaning: An activity done regularly in one's leisure time for pleasure.

learn.meaning: The action or skill of reading written matter.

learn.meaning: Vocal or instrumental sounds combined in a pleasing way.

learn.meaning: To engage in activity for enjoyment or sport.
learn.example: I like to play football on weekends.

learn.meaning: Look at or observe attentively over a period of time.

learn.meaning: Make a journey, typically of some length.

lessons.title: Workplace & Jobs

learn.meaning: An assembly of people for a professional discussion.

learn.meaning: A person responsible for controlling or administering an organization.

lessons.title: Making Plans
